en.headline: HKTDC lifts 2026 export growth forecast to 42-47 percent on AI demand
en.dek: The Trade Development Council said stronger-than-expected global appetite for semiconductors and electronics pushed first-eight-month growth to 42.5 percent.
body: The Hong Kong Trade Development Council on Monday substantially raised its full-year merchandise export growth forecast for 2026 to between 42 and 47 percent, citing robust artificial-intelligence-related demand.

Exports in the first eight months of the year rose 42.5 percent year-on-year. Electronics, which account for roughly 80 percent of total exports, grew 52.8 percent. Director of research Bruce Pang said demand for semiconductors, memory chips, computer components and telecommunications equipment expanded much faster than expected.

The council had previously projected growth of about 20 percent in June. Pang added that improved China-US relations had reduced the risk of further tariff escalation and that solid demand from the Chinese mainland and ASEAN markets should support performance through the rest of the year.

zh.headline: 貿發局上調今年出口增長預測至42%至47%
zh.dek: 受人工智能相關電子產品需求帶動，首八個月出口按年升42.5%，貿發局將全年預測大幅上調。
body: 香港貿易發展局周一大幅上調2026年商品出口增長預測至42%至47%，指全球對人工智能相關科技產品需求較預期強勁。
今年首八個月本港出口按年上升42.5%。電子產品佔總出口約八成，同期增長52.8%。研究總監彭文輝表示，半導體、記憶體晶片、電腦零部件及電訊設備需求增長遠超預期。
貿發局六月時預測增長約20%。彭文輝指近期中美關係發展有助改善貿易環境，降低關稅進一步升級風險，加上內地及東盟等主要市場需求穩健，預料餘下時間出口表現仍有支持。
